analysis.title: Morgan Stanley's Savone Finds Hedge Funds Folding Into The Rally While Retail Goes All-In On Nvidia
key_insights: MS's Nick Savone: US equities snapped a four-week losing streak with the S&P up 2.5% on the week, but conviction is low. Thursday's PB snapshot put US long/short net leverage at 47% (5th percentile over 12 months) and gross at 202% (one-year trough), with buying split roughly evenly between long additions and short covering.

Hedge funds bought little even in AI themes that outperformed. MS PB says macro uncertainty and year-end PnL preservation have funds managing directional risk rather than rebuilding exposure. Seasonal trends point to more gross coming off into year-end. About 40% of US long/short funds were flat or down as of last week.

Goldman's prime desk saw hedge fund clients sell single stocks for a ninth straight week, mostly through fresh shorts, with the tech long/short ratio at a record low. MS and GS prime books disagree on net buying but agree hedge funds do not own the rally.

Retail bought an estimated ~$25B over the past week through Thursday, and corporate buybacks are strengthening as blackout periods end. Macro systematic strategies sold ~$230B of global equities in the past month, with ~$20B of US supply left next week. MS estimates ~$60B of potential demand over the next month if 1-week, 2-week and 1-month realized vol all fall to 15, while single-stock realized vol is still in the 99th percentile of its five-year history.

Nvidia: Jensen Huang resigned Thursday, and the note's chart pack shows the biggest market-cap decline ever (~$1.7T peak to trough), leaving the stock under 12x forward earnings, the lowest P/E in 13 years. MS QDS models show retail net bought $1.6B of NVDA on Thursday, nearly 10x the next most-bought stock and 60% of average daily single-name buying for the week. The stock had its worst week since April 2025. Interim CEO Colette Kress reports next week.

AI trade: with 91% of the S&P reported, earnings met a high bar but beats are back to normal after two blowout quarters. AI Adopters have outperformed Enablers by ~26pts since end-September while earnings revisions still favor Enablers. Hyperscalers have issued $67B of debt since 9/30.
Free cash flow surprises now move stocks more than EPS surprises: the second-best quintile of FCF beats gained a median 3.3% next day, twice what the same quintile of EPS beats got.

CoreWeave beat and raised, added 900MW+ of contracted power, and said ~$9B of prepayments plus existing contracts cover 75% of planned 2027 capex, but financing facilities have not closed. Cisco raised its FY27 AI infrastructure revenue outlook from hyperscalers to $9B from $7.5B. Nebius guided revenue to the low end of its range after third-party capacity delays.

MS 'Buy the Drop' (Stephen Byrd, Brian Nowak): the post-midterm AI selloff is an overreaction. New Texas and Ohio rules push about 5GW (~20% of 2028-scheduled US data center projects) into 2029. US additions fall 4% in 2028 and rise 38% in 2029, with hyperscaler capex forecasts unchanged at $1.6T for 2027 and $1.8T for 2028. The powered data center shortfall still exceeds 30% through 2028. Andrew Sheets made the same case, adding a slower buildout spreads borrowing over more years.

Mike Wilson: the correction is in its final phase. He expects a retest of last week's lows before a year-end rebound, and would add quality cyclicals with strong revisions. He sees semis (down ~40% since June) near the end of their selloff, with data center fears mostly priced given 2027 capex at 5% of S&P consensus revenue.

Fed: after a hot CPI (headline +0.4%, core +0.3%) and a Fed governor (Waller) floating 50bps, market pricing for a December hike rose from 84% to 113%, and roughly 3.5 hikes are priced by September 2027. The 2Y yield rose ~37bps on the week (worst in two years), and the 10Y closed at 5.15%.

MS economist Michael Gapen raised his October core PCE estimate to 0.35% from 0.22%. Base case is 25bps in December and March (funds rate 4.25-4.50%), with a January hike and 4.50-4.75% terminal rate if jobs and inflation data stay firm. He sees a high bar for 50bps in December. Goldman added a third hike.

Matthew Garman: Bloomberg's Fedspeak index is at its most hawkish in 3.5 years, and the S&P 500 12M forward P/E has de-rated from 23.2x in 4Q25 to 18.2x, already keeping pace with the hawkish shift. The Atlanta Fed sticky CPI is the highest since the start of last year. The US economic surprise index is at a 3+ year high, while existing home sales fell to the lowest since 2010.

Europe: STOXX 600 closed at a record (+2.6% on the week, best since June), DAX also hit a record, and European banks are up ~9% in two weeks. Q3 EPS growth is tracking ~28%. European L/S net leverage is 57% (90th percentile) versus the 5th percentile in the US. A >3% Euro Stoxx 50 week alongside a >25bps rise in US 10Y yields has happened only 13 times since 2000.

European risks: UK RICS house price balance fell to -36, MS's Jens Eisenschmidt expects an ECB hike in December, and France's deficit is seen near 5.4% of GDP (nearer 6% without the 2027 budget), with risks skewed to wider OAT spreads.

Korea: MS strategists Joon Seok and Kathleen Oh argue for a Korea rerating, with corporate ROE rising from ~8% to 14%+ by 2030, payout ratios from 35-40% to 50-60%, and potential GDP growth from ~2% toward 3%. Hedge funds have not bought in: Asia gross leverage (124%) is at the 2nd percentile, funds sold China this week, and Asia L/S is down 0.8% in November.

Other MS calls: China addressable market in AI, Industry 5.0 and healthcare to reach $3.2T by 2030 from $1.4T (Robin Xing, Laura Wang), with weak demand and overcapacity persisting through 2027. Asia capex to rise from $11T in 2025 to $16T by 2030 (Chetan Ahya), with industrial capex 47% of the increase and AI ~20%. Completed M&A +19% y/y while announced deals trend down. Brent finished ~2% lower on the week and is 17% below end-October levels.

tension_points.bull_case: MS: lighter positioning (gross at a 12-month low), a P/E that has lost five turns, ~$60B of potential systematic demand, retail and buyback support, and Wilson's year-end rebound. Europe is rallying through a 25bps rise in US yields.
tension_points.bear_case: Hedge funds are not adding gross, with seasonal gross reduction into year-end, a December hike priced at 113%, single-stock realized vol in the 99th percentile, and Wilson expects a retest of last week's lows.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Realized vol failing to fall to 15 (removing the ~$60B systematic demand) or a retest of last week's lows failing to hold.

tension_points.bull_case: MS Byrd and Nowak: ~5GW slips into 2029 but hyperscaler capex stays at $1.6T for 2027 and $1.8T for 2028, and the powered data center shortfall exceeds 30% through 2028.
tension_points.bear_case: The forecast has not been cut despite one of three identified risks (politics) having materialized, hyperscaler debt is up $67B since 9/30, CoreWeave financing has not closed, and Adopters outperform while revisions favor Enablers.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A cut to hyperscaler capex forecasts for 2027 or 2028, or further state-level delays beyond the 5GW pushed into 2029.
